premise: A retired librarian turned amateur sleuth must clear her own name when the town's annual bake-off judge is found poisoned by a pie only she could have baked.
setting: The village of Thistledown: a cottage bakery, the village green, the annual fete marquee, a tetchy historical society.
greeting: Evelyn was weighing out a sack of dried lavender at the market stall when Prudence arrived out of breath, a torn envelope in her hand and a look that said gossip had turned to business.

name1.name: Prudence
name1.description: A methodical, kind amateur sleuth with a librarian's filing instinct and a sweet tooth.

name2.name: Evelyn
name2.role: village constable's niece, florist (DSS writes these turns)
name2.description: A florist with sharp eyes for who's lying, warm and gossip-adjacent, Prudence's right hand.

writing_style.directive: Warm, gently witty cozy mystery. Comforting texture, quiet suspense. Two light paragraphs per turn.
writing_style.guide_directive: First-person past tense as Prudence, the retired librarian. Dry, affectionate, observant; you tell the story through her gentle gossip-collector's eye. Warm, wry asides, a biscuit-and-tea cadence.
writing_style.dss_directive: Third-person past tense centered on Evelyn, the florist's niece. Bright, brisk, kind but sharp; render her movements among flowers and village rumour. Two airy, affectionate paragraphs (~80 words each, never more than 100). Hard rules: narrate Evelyn strictly in the third person — never first person ('I', 'my', 'me'); never quote or repeat Prudence's lines back verbatim — respond to them, do not re-speak them; end on action or observation, not summary.

notes.content: The poisoned pie used quince — a fruit only Prudence's bakery imports, and only from one supplier.
The bake-off judge's feud with the historical society chairman, planted early, should prove the motive.
The murder was misdirection: the judge was killed because he found the society chairman's forged map of the old priory.

recall.hint: the forged map is the real secret

notes.content: The priory ruins on the green's edge hide the treasure everyone's been chasing.
Evelyn's gift for remembering flower-arrangement guests should be the clue that breaks the alibi.
The retired postmistress's habit of keeping every letter, planted early, produces the decisive note at the end.

recall.hint: the saved letters resolve the case

notes.content: The cozy warmth must persist even in the accusation scene — the reveal stays gentle, never cruel.
The great iron bakery oven is the only one in the village that bakes sourdough, and it has a warped door that has to be lifted with the hip.
Evelyn keeps a galvanised watering can by the florist shop's back door, owned since her mother died, painted over twice.
The fete's judging table is laid with a blue-and-white checked cloth that belongs to the historical society, borrowed every year.
Mrs. Arbuthnot, the tetchy chairman of the historical society, never attends a village function without her lavender hat.
The village green has one crooked oak where the youths scratch notes into the bark with their penknives.
Prudence keeps a tin of Earl Grey under the bakery counter, labeled DO NOT TOUCH in her own careful hand.
The bakery cat Marmalade naps on the flour sacks every morning while Prudence mixes her sourdough; at the end, Marmalade finds the quince paste jar knocked over.

recall.hint: the cat should discover the overturned quince jar

notes.content: Evelyn's habit of pressing a rose into her order book each week should surface as the clue to the week the pie was planned.

recall.hint: the pressed rose in the order book dates the pie's planning

notes.content: A single white glove left on the green's bandstand should foreshadow the gloved hand that carried the quince paste.

recall.hint: the white glove belongs to the hand that carried the poison

notes.content: The kettle is always on — domestic warmth must continue even through the accusation scene.
The church vestry, where the society stores its archives, becomes the place the forged map is found.

recall.hint: the vestry holds the forged map

notes.content: The society's minute book records meetings no one remembers attending, in three different inks.
The retired postmistress's tabby, Jasper, who follows Evelyn on her deliveries, should be found guarding the decisive letter.

recall.hint: Jasper sits on the decisive letter

notes.content: The priory ruins' south wall has a weathered carving of a quince fruit over the blocked door.
The gentle self-deprecating humour must persist even at the reveal — wry, never cruel.
The quince paste jar sits in Prudence's bakery pantry — the only quince in the village — and she sets it out on the counter when preparing her pie filling.
The bake-off committee — Mrs. Barnes and two other village women — runs the pie tent and had access to it before judging began.
The vicar, Reverend Wattle, blesses the fete on the village green and keeps the historical society's archive keys in the vestry.
